title: Subnet hygiene, route healing, and endpoint-aware NAT/IGW Terraform module
creator: Sonia Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that codifies subnet naming/tagging conventions, route table reconciliation, endpoint-aware NAT/IGW attachment patterns, and automated healing for drifted routes and degraded gateway attachments. The module should support multi-AZ private deployments, allow per-environment overrides, emit health telemetry, and include a safe upgrade path (canary plan + rollback hooks) for customers using Redwood Private.
tasks: Design module API: inputs for subnet role mapping, AZ distribution, nat/igw preferences, endpoint whitelist prefix lists, route propagation flags.

Implement core resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet, aws_route_table, aws_route, aws_route_table_association, aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway, aws_eip, aws_vpc_endpoint, aws_route_propagation (or equivalent).
Add tagging and subnet hygiene enforcement: name, environment, role, zone, cost_center tags and validation warnings in plan output.
Route healing controller: Lambda (or small controller) that compares route tables against desired state and creates reconciliation drift plans; expose SQS/CloudWatch alarms for failures.
Health checks: synthetic probes that confirm NAT/IGW egress from each private subnet to telemetry endpoints and record to a dashboard.
Canary upgrade flow: terraform plan gating, staged apply across AZs, automated rollback hooks wired into the health checks.
Terraform tests: unit tests (terratest), integration in sandbox account, acceptance tests for failover scenarios.
Docs and examples: README, upgrade notes, migration guide for existing VPCs, example modules for single-AZ and 3-AZ topologies.
Add telemetry: emit metrics to Datadog/CloudWatch for NAT bandwidth, route flaps, endpoint connectivity, and module upgrade durations.
Security review: KMS usage for EIP metadata (where needed), IAM least privilege for the healing lambda/controller.
acceptance_criteria: Module creates VPC and subnets with consistent names/tags and outputs subnet IDs for workload wiring.
Route reconciliation job detects and repairs missing routes for expected endpoint prefixes within 5 minutes and logs actions.
NAT/IGW attachments can be provisioned per-AZ with fallback to cross-AZ NATs when preferred AZs are constrained.
Terraform plan contains clear warnings when a change will replace critical egress infrastructure and provides an automated canary strategy.
Health checks report per-subnet egress success rate and trigger automatic remediation for persistent failures.
Module includes example upgrade runbook and a validated canary apply that can be executed via CI with a single flag.
Unit and integration tests pass in the sandbox checkout and a tagged release is published to the internal module registry.
comments: 2026-02-20 Sonia Patel: Triage - customers deploying Redwood Private reported inconsistent subnet tag patterns and manual route fixes during upgrades. Proposal: a single module that enforces hygiene and provides automated healing.

2026-02-24 Ethan Murray: Arch review - prefer a lightweight Lambda reconciler over a long-running controller to reduce ops burden for private/on-prem setups. Will use SQS for queued reconciliation tasks.
2026-02-27 Design feedback: Add explicit support for VPC endpoints with prefix-list based routes for S3/Dynamo style endpoints; document trade-offs for gateway vs interface endpoints.
2026-03-01 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/ENG-204158-subnet-hygiene (WIP). Adding resources and terratest scaffold.
2026-03-03 Security: initial IAM policy reviewed; need to tighten Lambda role to only update route tables in tagged VPCs and to write to a dedicated CloudWatch log group.
2026-03-05 Ethan Murray: In-progress - implemented route reconciliation lambda and basic health probes. Next: add canary orchestration in CI and finalize docs.
risks: Automated route repairs could incorrectly modify customer route tables if tag-based scoping is wrong; mitigation: dry-run mode and manual approval for first fixes.
Canary applies add more CI complexity and possible state drift if partially applied; mitigation: strong idempotency and post-apply validation checks.
Lambda-based reconciler requires network reachability to metadata and telemetry endpoints in private networks; mitigation: allow customer-provided endpoints and fallbacks.
testing_plan: Unit tests: terratest staged for all resources including route additions and removals.
Integration: deploy module in sandbox VPC with 3 AZs, simulate IGW/NAT failure and validate route healing and failover.
Canary: CI job to apply changes to a single AZ, run health probes for 10 minutes, and automatically proceed or rollback based on thresholds.
Chaos test: periodic IGW/NAT detach simulations to verify reconciliation latency and idempotency.
